text:
maya: Ran canary for nebula-liteq-v2 (int8) on prod-like stack. Seeing ~1.7% funcall parse failures vs raven-3b baseline ~0.4%. canary id canary-2026-03-21-04
alex: examples? json malform or schema mismatch?
maya: small sample of outputs that failed parsing:
```
{"name": "update_user", "arguments": {"user_id": 123, "email": "a@example.com",}
```
and
```
{"name": "create_order", "args": [ {"sku": "X123"
```
logs: parse_error: JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string or unexpected trailing comma; schema_violation: missing 'args' field
ryan: did retries kick in? what's retry/backoff budget for canary?
maya: retries did run, retry rate for these invocations ~3x baseline. we used retry_budget=0.02, backoff=exp(0.2,2). tail latency doesn't move much. curl we used:
```
curl -XPOST https://canary.redwood/api/invoke -d '{"model":"nebula-liteq-v2","prompt":...}'
```
ci-bot: Canary summary: 10k invocations, parse_fail=1.7%, timeout=0.2%, avg_tok_latency=21ms; artifacts: https://ci/internal/canary/6378901234 :thumbsup:
sam: try quick mitigation: server-side wrap -> respond with `{"result": <model_output>}` so JSON parser sees single top-level value. also try temp->0.0 and disable streaming. can you A/B that?
maya: ran wrap+temp0 test on 2k inits: parse_fail -> 0.6% (big win). still ~0.15% are truncated suffixes that look like kv-cache/batch boundary issues. attaching example:
```
..."args": ["item"], "meta": "ok"  <-- then cut off abruptly
```
ryan: that sounds like tokenizer alignment / batch splitting. nebula-liteq's decoder kernel introduced a new fast chunker last month; it may not flush partial buffers on some batch edge-cases.
ryan: quick mitigation: enable `ctx_pad=32` and set header `X-Serve-Heuristic: suffix-sentinel` which inserts an EOS sentinel when streaming finishes. canary patch below:
```
PATCH /serve/config
{ "model":"nebula-liteq-v2", "heuristics": {"ctx_pad":32, "emit_eos_sentinel":true}}
```
maya: applying patch to canary now.
ops-bot: Scheduled config patch to canary-2026-03-21-04 at 06:15 UTC
maya: after patch run (5k invocations) parse_fail=0.45% -- almost baseline. retries back down to 1.1x. leaving more exhaustive run for tomorrow.
alex: good catch. let's put this in onboarding checklist: ensure quant decoder kernel respects stream flush and add `emit_eos_sentinel` as default for int8 builds until we fix kernel.
ryan: I'll open runtime PR to add explicit flush on batch_end and a test for truncated suffixes.
maya: filing ticket now: https://redwood/issue/ML-5234 - includes canary artifacts and samples. ping me if you need sample payloads.
alex: thanks all. follow up in eng-runtime standup tomorrow.
